source.title: Effective non-linear dynamics of binary condensates and open problems

accepted.question_text: For the two-species Bose gas in the Gross-Pitaevskii scaling considered in this paper, can one remove the positivity assumption on the interaction potentials and still rigorously derive persistence of two-component condensation together with the effective coupled Gross-Pitaevskii system? Equivalently, can the theorem proved here under positive, spherically symmetric, compactly supported interaction potentials be extended to allow non-positive interactions at the true Gross-Pitaevskii scaling, rather than only in softer scaling regimes?

evidence.quote: Conversely, the removal of the positivity condition is an important open problem in the subject; in [19], it is proven positivity can be removed for a much softer scaling than the one in (21).

accepted.question_text: For a spin-1 Bose condensate with spin-spin interaction, the paper writes down the effective three-component nonlinear Schrödinger system (58). Can one rigorously derive that system of equations from the underlying many-body quantum dynamics of the spinor condensate?

evidence.quote: The rigorous derivation of the system (58) from many-body quantum dynamics is undoubtedly one of the next frontiers in the mathematics of the Bose gas.

accepted.question_text: For a one-component Bose gas, can one rigorously derive the Gross-Pitaevskii equation i∂_t u_t = -∆u_t + 8πa|u_t|^2u_t from the many-body quantum dynamics in the Gross-Pitaevskii scaling?

evidence.quote: The one-component problem, namely the derivation of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation i∂tut = −∆ut +8πa|ut|2ut, has been an important open problem in mathematical physics in recent years. It was first solved by Erd"os, Schlein and Yau in 2006 (see [4] and [5]); their proof was based on the BBGKY formalism and did not provide a convergence rate.
